text:
Can you write the pitch for our crowdfunding campaign? I chair the volunteer group trying to reopen the one-screen cinema in our town of 6,500. It closed in 2022.

Facts:
- We need $85,000 to replace the projector and sound system and fix the roof. The building's owner has agreed to rent it to us for $1 a year for 10 years if we raise it.
- We ran a campaign 3 years ago for $120,000. It reached $47,000 and we refunded everyone.
- This time a local bank has pledged $25,000 if we raise the rest by June 30.
- 46 volunteers have signed up to run the box office and the snack bar.
- When it closed, the cinema was selling about 180 tickets a week.
- The nearest other cinema is 38 miles away.

Keep it under 350 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. Each answer would change what the pitch says.

1. **What's different from last time, and why do you think the first campaign fell short?** Many backers will remember getting refunded, so the pitch needs to deal with that directly. I can already point to a lower target, the bank's pledge, the $1 lease and the 46 volunteers. Is there anything else, like a new board, a clearer plan, or a cheaper approach to the roof?

2. **How will the cinema pay its way once it's open?** People will want to know it won't close again in two years. Do you have rough running costs, ticket prices, or a break-even figure (e.g. "we need X tickets a week; we used to sell 180")?

3. **What are the mechanics?** I assume the deadline is June 30, 2027, and that the crowd needs to raise $60,000 to unlock the bank's $25,000. Is that right? Is the campaign all-or-nothing again, with refunds if you miss? And are there reward tiers I should mention?

4. **What are the names?** I need the cinema's name, the town's name and the bank's name, if the bank is happy to be named.

5. **Is there one story or detail that sums up what the cinema meant to the town?** For example, a long-running Saturday matinee, a first date that became a marriage, or what people do now instead of making the 38-mile drive.

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll write without them rather than guess.

1. Three local businesses have already pledged $11,000 in writing, so we're not starting from zero. We'll also post a public spending report every three months at the town library. I don't really know why the first campaign fell short.

2. I don't have running costs, ticket prices or a break-even figure.

3. Yes, June 30, 2027, and the campaign opens May 1. We need $60,000 outside the bank's $25,000. The businesses' $11,000 counts toward that. It's all-or-nothing again: if we don't reach $85,000 by June 30, every pledge is returned in full. I don't know about reward tiers yet.

4. The cinema is the Majestic on Main Street. Please leave the town and bank names out for now.

5. Nothing specific comes to mind, so write it without one.

<final_document>
**Bring Back the Majestic**

The Majestic on Main Street closed in 2022. Since then, seeing a film on a big screen has meant a 76-mile round trip, because the nearest cinema is 38 miles away.

We're a group of volunteers working to reopen it. We need $85,000 to replace the projector and sound system and to fix the roof.

**You may remember our last attempt.**
Three years ago we asked for $120,000. We reached $47,000, fell short and refunded every pledge in full. This campaign is built differently:

- **A smaller target:** $85,000, not $120,000.
- **A lease ready to sign:** Once we raise the money, the building's owner will rent us the Majestic for $1 a year for ten years.
- **A bank behind us:** A local bank has pledged $25,000 if we raise the rest by June 30, 2027.
- **A head start:** Three local businesses have already pledged $11,000 in writing.
- **People ready to work:** 46 volunteers have signed up to run the box office and the snack bar.

That leaves **$49,000** to raise from the community. Last time, our community pledged $47,000. We're asking you to do it again and go a little further.

**Your money is safe either way.**
The campaign is all-or-nothing. If we don't reach the full $85,000 by June 30, every pledge will be returned in full, as it was last time. If we do reach it, we'll post a public spending report at the town library every three months, so you can see where every dollar went.

**The audience is here.**
When the Majestic closed, it was still selling about 180 tickets a week. That's an audience that has been waiting for a screen.

The campaign runs from May 1 to June 30, 2027. Pledge what you can, tell your neighbours, and help us turn the lights back on at the Majestic.
</final_document>

Some notes on the choices I made:

- **The $49,000 figure is the core of the pitch.** It's the $85,000 total minus the bank's $25,000 and the businesses' $11,000. It's only $2,000 more than the town pledged last time, which makes the goal feel within reach. Please check the sum before it goes out.
- **The pitch doesn't explain why the first campaign failed,** since you don't know. Instead it lists what has changed.
- **There are no claims about running costs or long-term sustainability.** You don't have those figures yet, so the only evidence of demand is the 180 tickets a week. Expect backers to ask how the cinema will pay its way. A rough break-even number would make a strong addition before May 1.
- **Reward tiers, the town name and the bank name** can all go in later without restructuring. The draft is about 300 words, so there's room.
